Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: Côte d'Ivoire has a general consumer protection law ("loi relative à la consommation") applicable to consumer transactions, and the World Bank DFS regulatory framework note indicates financial consumer protection requirements exist in e‑money and payments rules (e.g., disclosure/complaints) alongside national consumer protection law; this supports a 'partial' payment consumer protection framework (general + sector rules, but not evidenced as a single comprehensive payments-specific statute in sources reviewed).
revision_notes: Original score (2=Partial) rested on the 2017 World Bank DFS regulatory note and Côte d'Ivoire's general consumer law. Fetched and read BCEAO Instruction No. 001-01-2024 (23 January 2024, applicable to Côte d'Ivoire as a UMOA member state), which contains dedicated payment consumer protection provisions: a mandatory client complaints-handling mechanism as a licensing condition (Art. 51), liability allocation for unauthorised payment transactions (Art. 69), and mandatory professional indemnity insurance or financial guarantee covering losses from unauthorised access to payment account data (Art. 12). This sits alongside the UMOA banking law's Article 23 on pricing transparency and user protection. Together these constitute a comprehensive, payment-specific consumer protection framework rather than only partial/general coverage, so the score is recalculated to 3=Yes. This is a promotion to the top of the scale and is flagged for human review.
revised_comments: BCEAO Instruction No. 001-01-2024 on payment services, applicable to Côte d'Ivoire as a UMOA member state, requires payment institutions to maintain a client complaints-handling mechanism (Article 51), sets out provider liability for unauthorised payment transactions (Article 69), and requires professional indemnity insurance or a financial guarantee covering losses from unauthorised access to payment account data (Article 12). This sits alongside the general consumer protection law (loi relative à la consommation) and the UMOA banking law's transparency and user-protection provisions (Article 23), together forming a comprehensive, payment-specific consumer protection framework.

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: Sources reviewed indicate Côte d'Ivoire's Law No. 2013‑450 does not stipulate a breach notification protocol (no notification to DPA or data subjects specified), so breach notification is not mandatory under the cited privacy-law summaries.
revision_notes: Original score (1=No) rested solely on a summary of Loi n°2013-450 (general data protection law), which indeed contains no breach-notification clause; this remains correct as far as it goes. However, fetched and read BCEAO Instruction No. 001-03-2021 (Art. 10), which obliges payment service providers and market-infrastructure operators to notify the BCEAO within 24 hours of any incident causing over two hours of service interruption, followed by a detailed report within three calendar days, with penalties under Art. 11 for late compliance. BCEAO Instruction No. 001-01-2024 defines 'incident opérationnel majeur' to explicitly include breaches compromising the confidentiality of information systems and data. Together these constitute a mandatory regulatory incident/breach-notification requirement not captured in the original source set, so the score is recalculated to 3=Mandatory. This is a promotion to the top of the scale and is flagged for human review.
revised_comments: BCEAO Instruction No. 001-03-2021 on the oversight of financial market infrastructures and payment instruments and services requires payment service providers to report to the BCEAO, within 24 hours, any incident causing a service interruption of more than two hours, followed by a detailed report within three calendar days; non-compliance is subject to penalties. BCEAO Instruction No. 001-01-2024 on payment services defines a 'major operational incident' to include breaches compromising the confidentiality of information systems and data. Together these instruments establish a mandatory regulatory incident- and breach-notification requirement for payment service providers operating in Côte d'Ivoire.
